answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, non-reusable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A reputation ledger ties payouts to that bond’s history; proven fraud burns the stake and voids pending rewards, while honest agents recover it after a delay. This makes a nebula of disposable accounts costly: an attacker must fund every sybil and risk losing each bond. A cipher can protect private credentials, and an orchard of agents can still join, but neither creates free identities.
